endonym.gloss: the frame that is read by hand

description.value: A hanging frame of ninety-odd mineral tubes of graded length, lashed in four ranks, in which the household's side of the fall account is held by the position and spacing of the tubes rather than by anything cut into them. It is read by running a limb across the ranks, which is also how it is corrected, and in a current it makes a low rattle that a household can hear from its own doorway. This one hung at the ninth rib from about 2260 and was replaced in 2302 after a rank came adrift. Eleven tubes are cracked and two ranks have been relashed with newer cord.

notes.value: The accompanying record is a tube-by-tube reading given by the house account holder in 2303, and it includes the entry for a Consortium sample line lost from Station Two, which the house entered as a fall. The station has not worked out whether the entry can be closed and has not asked.
